skill.name: prisma-next-debug
skill.description: Diagnose Prisma Next CLI, runtime, migration, contract, and SQL errors from structured envelopes and route each code to a documented recovery.
skill.summary: Route Prisma Next error codes and symptoms to focused recovery steps.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: Static analysis misidentified Markdown inline-code formatting as executable shell syntax. The skill is documentation-only, but it recommends a command that can apply destructive database changes without explicit approval.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before db update, migrate, db sign, or any -y operation. Recommend a dry run and verified backup first.

content.value_statement: Prisma Next failures expose detailed envelopes that can be difficult to route correctly. This skill maps codes, metadata, and symptoms to focused recovery steps.
actual_capabilities: Distinguishes CLI, runtime, and SQL driver error shapes.
Routes stable Prisma Next codes to documented recovery actions.
Checks wrapped PN-RUN-3000 errors for the original meta.code value.
Diagnoses client shutdown, hanging scripts, and capability-related type errors.
Explains current alternatives for Studio, query logging, and EXPLAIN workflows.
limitations: Does not replace Prisma Next authoring skills for queries, contracts, or migrations.
Requires the full error envelope for reliable routing.
Cannot inspect a live database unless the user provides relevant diagnostic output.
Does not provide a built-in Studio, query logger, or plan EXPLAIN API.

use_cases.title: Route a CLI failure
use_cases.description: Identify the envelope code, severity, and metadata, then select the matching recovery path.

use_cases.title: Recover a migration
use_cases.description: Interpret migration wrappers, hash mismatches, drift, and marker diagnostics before choosing the next command.

use_cases.title: Diagnose runtime behavior
use_cases.description: Separate query, capability, budget, cancellation, and client lifecycle failures during incident response.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an error
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this Prisma Next error envelope and give the safest next step: [paste envelope].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner diagnosis of one complete error envelope.

prompt_templates.title: Route a wrapped error
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this PN-RUN-3000 envelope, including meta.code, and identify the correct recovery workflow: [paste envelope].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate diagnosis of a wrapped migration or runtime error.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze migration state
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this migration status output with the contract hash and propose non-destructive verification steps: [paste output and context].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration drift and marker analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Build a recovery plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized recovery plan from these CLI, runtime, and SQL errors. Separate safe checks from commands requiring approval: [paste evidence].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced incident analysis across multiple failure surfaces.

output_examples.input: A runtime envelope reports BUDGET.TIME_EXCEEDED with a strict latency limit.
output_examples.output: Category: budget enforcement. Review query cost and the configured latency budget before increasing the threshold. Re-run the same workload after one controlled change.

output_examples.input: A migration command returns PN-RUN-3000 and reports MIGRATION.HASH_MISMATCH in its metadata.
output_examples.output: The outer code is a wrapper. The metadata identifies a migration hash mismatch. Re-emit the named migration, inspect the resulting diff, and verify state before applying changes.

output_examples.input: A script prints query results but does not exit, and db.end is unavailable.
output_examples.output: The Prisma Next client uses db.close for teardown. Close it after all queries complete. Do not close a shared client inside a request handler.

best_practices: Provide the complete envelope, including code, severity, fix, metadata, and location.
Use dry-run or verification commands before any operation that changes database state.
Redact credentials and sensitive data from connection strings and diagnostic output.
anti_patterns: Do not route only from the human summary or process exit code.
Do not ignore meta.code when PN-RUN-3000 wraps the original failure.
Do not bypass destructive-operation confirmation without explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which error formats can this skill interpret?
faq.answer: It covers Prisma Next CLI envelopes, runtime envelopes, SQL driver errors, and selected TypeScript symptoms.

faq.question: What should I provide for the best diagnosis?
faq.answer: Provide JSON or verbose output with code, severity, why, fix, metadata, and location fields.

faq.question: Does it execute recovery commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends recovery steps. Commands that modify database state require explicit review and approval.

faq.question: Can it diagnose PN-RUN-3000 errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks meta.code for the original migration or runtime failure before selecting a recovery path.

faq.question: Can it replace Prisma Studio?
faq.answer: No. Prisma Next has no first-party Studio. Use schema output or an approved database client.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Redact passwords, tokens, and connection details before sharing envelopes, command output, or configuration.
